items.prompt: A has rows (4, 1) and (2, 3). What is the top-left entry of A³?
items.hint: You can multiply A by itself three times, or use A³ = P D³ P⁻¹.
items.explain: Raising D to the third power cubes each eigenvalue on its diagonal, and P D³ P⁻¹ then has the top-left entry {answer}, the same as multiplying A by itself three times.

items.prompt: A table of year-to-year rates between a few groups is applied 20 years in a row. Which idea makes the 20-year result easy to compute?

choices.why: Only the diagonal entries are raised to the 20th power, and P and P⁻¹ switch into and out of the eigenvector directions.
The trace is one number from the diagonal; it does not give the 20-year table.
The determinant tells how areas scale, not what the table becomes after repeated years.

items.prompt: Before you continue, predict: can the shear with rows (1, 1) and (0, 1) be written as P D P⁻¹?
items.reasoning: No. It has only one eigenvector direction, so there are not enough independent eigenvectors to fill the columns of P, and P would have no inverse.
